question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's entrenched control over the Chinese Communist Party apparatus, including the Politburo Standing Committee and Central Military Commission, underpins the 95.9% trader consensus against removal before 2027. Loyal appointees dominate key posts following recent leadership adjustments, with no scheduled party congress or institutional mechanism for transition until the expected 21st Congress in autumn 2027. Public continuity in appearances and policy execution through mid-2026 shows no factional challenges or health indicators capable of prompting elite realignment. Low-probability shifts could still arise from an unforeseen medical event, acute economic pressures fostering internal consensus for change, or a destabilizing external crisis before year-end.

Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez holds the lead amid strong progressive visibility and New Hampshire poll mentions, while Gavin Newsom draws support from his California governorship and Jon Ossoff benefits from his Georgia Senate seat in a swing state.
